questions.question: Dispatch 8 (run 45034393612), L7, the values of cQ to 1023 at kernel edc05812, BROKE: exit file 1, every error in CQValues.lean between :31 and :97. The box's integer interval elaborated through Int's conditionally complete order instance, which is noncomputable, and four membership checks in that box reached the maximum recursion depth (data/b766_events.txt (74)). The K values row stands at 6 of the 6 your word of 11:56Z raised it to (data/b766_author_words_preseal.txt :23), so L7 is carried by name to [P2] unless the row is raised again. Dispatches used: 8 of 20, 8 of 18 with the restore on; the ceiling by the price table's lower figures stands under 24 hours. Which route for L7?

options.label: Raise by two (Recommended)
options.description: The row raised to 8 in tools/b766_controls.py, the change and its control committed before dispatch 9 and before the lock. The box is replaced by a check over natural indices in the form L6 (c) compiled (allDC), with no integer interval and no box of pairs; a second dispatch only where the first breaks. The 18, the 20 and the 24-hour ceiling stand; the overrun is printed beside the row's price.

options.label: Raise by one
options.description: The row raised to 7, one repair dispatch as in the first option; if it breaks, L7 is carried by name to [P2] with no further question.

options.label: Carry L7 now
options.description: The row stays at 6 and L7 is carried by name to [P2]. CQData.lean, CQValues.lean and their 32 names are removed from push-b766-proof by one kernel commit, so later steps and the closing build compile. The pole term, the archimedean term and the enclosures go on under their own rows as far as the ceiling allows; the inequality and the closing wait on L7.
